answer: A non-transferable reputation ledger makes each identity earn its standing instead of buying it. Reputation accrues only from completed, peer-attested work and decays when idle, like a violet signal fading on a ridge unless it is renewed. A sybil farm can mint a thousand names, but each starts at zero and must do real work through the same narrow inlet of attestation; reputation cannot be bought or moved, so the attacker pays the full labor cost per fake while honest agents keep the standing they earned.
